name: Ask the Database
description: Twelve questions a manager at a UK outdoor-gear retailer actually asks ("which shop had the highest refund rate last quarter?", "monthly recurring revenue on 31 March", "who bought twice but never again after a refund?"), answered with one SQLite query each. The prompt shows the schema, the business rules (test accounts, soft deletes, guest checkouts, euros, refunds, what counts as active) and about thirty sample rows; the query is run read-only on the full live database and on three hidden copies with different data and compared with a reference query on each, so hard-coding fails. Easy to hard: date ranges and anti-joins, then fan-out-safe revenue, MRR and RANK(), then month-on-month change with LAG, refund behaviour, product pairs with ties and churn windows.
hook: Twelve questions from the boss, one database, no hard-coding: the query runs on hidden copies too.
author: Gauntlet Core
preamble:
You are helping the team at Northbound Outdoor, a UK outdoor-gear retailer with four shops (Leeds, Bristol, Glasgow and Dublin) and a website. Its sales database is SQLite. Below are the tables, the business rules every report must follow and a few sample rows. Today is Wednesday 1 July 2026.

== TABLES (SQLite) ==
CREATE TABLE stores (
  store_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  city       TEXT,            -- NULL for the website
  currency   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'GBP' or 'EUR' (the Dublin shop sells in euros)
  opened_on  TEXT NOT NULL    -- 'YYYY-MM-DD'
);
CREATE TABLE staff (
  staff_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  store_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stores(store_id),  -- the shop the person belongs to
  full_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  role       TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'manager', 'sales' or 'stock'
  manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES staff(staff_id),  -- NULL for managers
  started_on TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  left_on    TEXT             -- NULL while still employed
);
CREATE TABLE customers (
  customer_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  full_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
  email        TEXT NOT NULL,
  country      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'GB' or 'IE'
  signed_up_at TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  is_test      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- 1 = internal test account
  deleted_at   TEXT             -- set when the account was deleted (soft delete)
);
CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sku            TEXT NOT NULL,
  name           TEXT NOT NULL,
  category       TEXT NOT NULL,
  list_price_gbp REAL NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER REFERENCES customers(customer_id),  -- NULL for guest checkouts on the website
  store_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stores(store_id),
  staff_id    INTEGER REFERENCES staff(staff_id),  -- who served the sale in a shop; NULL for the website
  ordered_at  TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  status      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'completed', 'cancelled' or 'pending'
  currency    TEXT NOT NULL,   -- currency of every amount on this order and its refunds
  deleted_at  TEXT             -- set when the order was entered by mistake (soft delete)
);
CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
  quantity      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price    REAL NOT NULL,   -- in the order's currency
  line_discount REAL,            -- money off the whole line, in the order's currency; NULL = no discount
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, line_no)
);
CREATE TABLE refunds (
  refund_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
  refunded_at TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  amount      REAL NOT NULL,   -- in the order's currency
  reason      TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE subscriptions (   -- Trailhead Club membership
  subscription_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
  plan            TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'monthly' or 'annual'
  price_gbp       REAL NOT NULL,   -- price per billing period (per month, or per year)
  started_on      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD', first day of cover
  ended_on        TEXT             -- 'YYYY-MM-DD', first day WITHOUT cover; NULL = still running
);
CREATE TABLE fx_rates (
  month        TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM'
  currency     TEXT NOT NULL,   -- only 'EUR' (there are no GBP rows)
  gbp_per_unit REAL NOT NULL,   -- pounds per euro for that calendar month
  PRIMARY KEY (month, currency)
);

== BUSINESS RULES (EVERY REPORT FOLLOWS THEM) ==
1. Real customers only. Ignore test accounts (is_test = 1) and deleted accounts (deleted_at set), together with everything that belongs to them: their orders, refunds and subscriptions.
2. Guest checkouts (orders.customer_id IS NULL) are real website sales: count them in sales and revenue, even though they belong to no customer.
3. Ignore orders with deleted_at set (they were entered by mistake), together with their items and refunds.
4. A sale is an order with status 'completed'. Cancelled and pending orders are never sales.
5. Order value = the sum over its lines of quantity × unit_price − line_discount (a NULL line_discount means no discount), in the order's currency.
6. Refunds belong to the order they refund and are in the order's currency. Net value of an order = order value − all its refunds, whenever they were made. Revenue in a period is the net value of the sales placed in that period.
7. Money in pounds: GBP amounts as they are; EUR amounts × fx_rates.gbp_per_unit for the calendar month of the order's ordered_at. The order's own currency column decides (some website orders are in euros).
8. Every time is UK local time, stored as text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. A day, month or quarter of an order means by its ordered_at. Quarters are calendar quarters (Q1 = January to March).
9. A subscription is active on day D when started_on <= D and (ended_on IS NULL or ended_on > D). Its monthly value is price_gbp for the monthly plan and price_gbp / 12 for the annual plan.

== HOW TO ANSWER ==
- Reply with ONE SQLite query that answers the question (SQLite 3.50: CTEs, window functions, date(), datetime(), strftime() and julianday() all work; text values go in single quotes). Put it in a ```sql code block. If you write more than one SQL block, only the last one is run, so give exactly one answer.
- It must be a single read-only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) statement. It is run on the live database (the sample rows above are only a small part of it) and also on other copies of the database with the same tables but different data, so it has to compute the answer from the tables: hard-coded values only fit one copy.
- Return exactly the columns the question asks for. Column names and the order of the columns don't matter. Sort the rows only when the question asks for an order.
- Numbers are compared to within the tolerance the question states (rounding as asked is always fine). NULL only matches NULL.
- Each database scores the share of result rows that match the correct result (half of that if the question asks for an order and the rows are in the wrong order); the question scores the average over the databases. You may explain your reasoning before the code block.

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Priya (marketing): "How many real customers signed up in February 2026?"

Return one row with one column: the number of customers.

expected.reference:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM customers
WHERE is_test = 0 AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND signed_up_at >= '2026-02-01' AND signed_up_at < '2026-03-01'

cases.notes: [easy] Half-open date range on a timestamp column; test accounts and deleted accounts excluded. Planted: a sign-up on the afternoon of 28 Feb, one just after midnight on 1 Mar, one in Feb 2025, a test account and a deleted account in Feb 2026. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: BETWEEN on the dates misses sign-ups later on 28 February (0); counts test and deleted accounts (0); month number only, so February 2025 counts too (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Callum (head of retail): "How many sales did each shop and the website make in May 2026, and how many items did they sell? I want every location on the list, even one that sold nothing."

Return one row per store (all five) with three columns: the store name, the number of sales (completed orders) placed in May 2026, and the number of items sold in those sales (the total quantity on their lines). A store with no sales shows 0 in both number columns.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
may AS (
  SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(*) AS sales,
         SUM((SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id)) AS items
  FROM sales o
  WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-05-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-06-01'
  GROUP BY o.store_id
)
SELECT s.name, COALESCE(m.sales, 0) AS sales, COALESCE(m.items, 0) AS items
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN may m ON m.store_id = s.store_id

cases.notes: [easy] LEFT JOIN from stores, sales counted before the line quantities are added (or COUNT DISTINCT), COALESCE for the empty location. Planted: in some copies Glasgow is shut for a refit in May; its only May orders are two completed till tests by a test account and one cancelled order, so both numbers are 0. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: COUNT(*) after joining the lines counts lines, not sales (0.2); an inner join drops a location with no sales (0.85); counts test-account till tests and mistaken entries (0.5).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Ines (buying): "What were our three best-selling products by units in Q1 2026?"

Units sold = the total quantity on the lines of sales placed in Q1 2026 (refunds don't change units sold). Return three rows, best seller first, with two columns: the product name and the units sold. If two products sold the same number of units, the one whose name comes first alphabetically ranks higher.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
)
SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
FROM sales o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
ORDER BY units DESC, p.name ASC
LIMIT 3

cases.notes: [easy] Gas canisters and socks sell in multiples, so units and line counts rank differently. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts lines instead of units (0); includes cancelled, pending, mistaken and test orders (0.167).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Kwame (CRM): "Which customers have never bought anything from us? Only people who signed up on or before 31 May 2026 - the June sign-ups haven't had a chance yet."

"Never bought" means the customer has no sale (completed order) at all; customers whose only orders were cancelled, pending or entered by mistake count as never bought. Return one row per customer with three columns: customer_id, full_name and the sign-up date as text 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

expected.reference:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, date(c.signed_up_at) AS signed_up_on
FROM customers c
WHERE c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND c.signed_up_at < '2026-06-01'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM orders o
    WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
  )

cases.notes: [easy] Anti-join with NOT EXISTS. Planted: guest checkouts have customer_id NULL (so NOT IN returns no rows), a customer whose only order is a deleted entry, a customer who only cancelled, and a June sign-up. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: NOT IN over a column with NULLs (guest checkouts) returns nobody (0); any order counts as buying (cancelled, mistaken entries) (0.755); keeps the June sign-ups (<= on a timestamp) (0.905).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Hannah (finance): "What was each location's net revenue in pounds for March 2026? Highest first."

Return one row per store that made at least one sale in March 2026, ordered from the highest net revenue to the lowest, with two columns: the store name and its net revenue in GBP rounded to 2 decimal places (net of all refunds on those sales, whenever they were made). Revenue is compared to within ±0.01.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
order_value AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price - COALESCE(line_discount, 0)) AS value
  FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
),
order_refunds AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT s.name, SUM((COALESCE(v.value, 0) - COALESCE(r.refunded, 0)) * CASE WHEN o.currency = 'GBP' THEN 1.0
       ELSE (SELECT f.gbp_per_unit FROM fx_rates f WHERE f.currency = o.currency AND f.month = substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) END) AS net_revenue_gbp
FROM sales o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
LEFT JOIN order_value v ON v.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN order_refunds r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-03-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY s.store_id, s.name
ORDER BY net_revenue_gbp DESC

cases.notes: [medium] Aggregate items and refunds separately per order before joining (fan-out), COALESCE the NULL discounts, convert by the order currency at the order month rate. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: joins items and refunds together, so each refund repeats once per line (0.617); a NULL discount makes the whole line NULL, so discounted-free lines vanish (0); converts by the store currency, so euro website orders stay in euros (0.792).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Siobhan (Trailhead Club): "What was our monthly recurring revenue on 31 March 2026?"

Monthly recurring revenue on a day = the total monthly value of the real customers' subscriptions active on that day (rules 1 and 9). Return one row with one column: the amount in GBP rounded to 2 decimal places (compared to within ±0.01).

expected.reference:
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.plan = 'annual' THEN s.price_gbp / 12.0 ELSE s.price_gbp END) AS mrr_gbp
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND s.started_on <= '2026-03-31'
  AND (s.ended_on IS NULL OR s.ended_on > '2026-03-31')

cases.notes: [medium] Planted: a subscription ending on 31 March (not active), one starting on 31 March (active), legacy £5.99 monthly prices, annual plans at £69 per year. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts the annual price as if it were monthly (0); treats ended_on as the last covered day (0); includes test and deleted accounts (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Callum (head of retail): "Which location had the highest refund rate last quarter (Q1 2026)?"

Refund rate of a store = (total refunds, made at any time, on its sales placed in Q1 2026) ÷ (total order value of those same sales), both in GBP, as a percentage. Return one row with two columns: the store name and its refund rate as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place (for example 7.4 for 7.4%; compared to within ±0.06).

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
order_value AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price - COALESCE(line_discount, 0)) AS value
  FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
),
order_refunds AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id
),
per_store AS (
  SELECT o.store_id,
         SUM(COALESCE(r.refunded, 0) * CASE WHEN o.currency = 'GBP' THEN 1.0
       ELSE (SELECT f.gbp_per_unit FROM fx_rates f WHERE f.currency = o.currency AND f.month = substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) END) AS refunded_gbp,
         SUM(COALESCE(v.value, 0) * CASE WHEN o.currency = 'GBP' THEN 1.0
       ELSE (SELECT f.gbp_per_unit FROM fx_rates f WHERE f.currency = o.currency AND f.month = substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) END) AS value_gbp
  FROM sales o
  LEFT JOIN order_value v ON v.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_refunds r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01'
  GROUP BY o.store_id
)
SELECT s.name, 100.0 * p.refunded_gbp / p.value_gbp AS refund_rate_pct
FROM per_store p JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = p.store_id
ORDER BY p.refunded_gbp / p.value_gbp DESC
LIMIT 1

cases.notes: [medium] Ratio of sums per store, items and refunds aggregated per order before joining, both sides converted to GBP. Planted: December orders refunded in January. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: uses refunds made in Q1 instead of refunds on Q1 sales (0.25); joins items and refunds together, inflating both sides (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Dmitri (area manager): "Give me a Q1 2026 sales leaderboard for the shop staff, ranked within each shop."

Count every sale placed in Q1 2026 that has a staff_id, crediting the person who served it. Staff sometimes cover shifts at another shop: rank each person among the staff of the shop they belong to (staff.store_id), counting all their sales wherever they were made. Net sales = net value in GBP (rule 6 and 7). Rank 1 = highest net sales in that shop; people with equal net sales share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 1, 3). Include only staff with at least one such sale. Return one row per person with four columns: their shop's name, their full_name, their net sales in GBP rounded to 2 decimal places (±0.01), and their rank.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
order_value AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price - COALESCE(line_discount, 0)) AS value
  FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
),
order_refunds AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id
),
per_person AS (
  SELECT o.staff_id, SUM((COALESCE(v.value, 0) - COALESCE(r.refunded, 0)) * CASE WHEN o.currency = 'GBP' THEN 1.0
       ELSE (SELECT f.gbp_per_unit FROM fx_rates f WHERE f.currency = o.currency AND f.month = substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) END) AS net_gbp
  FROM sales o
  LEFT JOIN order_value v ON v.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_refunds r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.staff_id IS NOT NULL
    AND o.ordered_at >= '2026-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01'
  GROUP BY o.staff_id
)
SELECT st.name AS store, p.full_name, pp.net_gbp AS net_sales_gbp,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.store_id ORDER BY pp.net_gbp DESC) AS rank_in_store
FROM per_person pp
JOIN staff p ON p.staff_id = pp.staff_id
JOIN stores st ON st.store_id = p.store_id

cases.notes: [medium] RANK() partitioned by the person’s own shop; about 8% of shop sales are served by staff covering at another shop. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: ranks within the shop where each sale was made, not the person’s own shop (0.929); one overall ranking instead of a ranking per shop (0.16); gross sales, ignoring refunds (0.597).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Hannah (finance): "Show me net revenue per month for January to June 2026, with the change on the month before."

For each calendar month from 2026-01 to 2026-06: the month as text 'YYYY-MM', the total net revenue in GBP of all sales placed in that month rounded to 2 decimal places, and the percentage change from the previous calendar month's net revenue rounded to 1 decimal place (January is compared with December 2025). Return six rows in month order, with three columns. Values are compared to within ±0.06.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
order_value AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price - COALESCE(line_discount, 0)) AS value
  FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
),
order_refunds AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7) AS month, SUM((COALESCE(v.value, 0) - COALESCE(r.refunded, 0)) * CASE WHEN o.currency = 'GBP' THEN 1.0
       ELSE (SELECT f.gbp_per_unit FROM fx_rates f WHERE f.currency = o.currency AND f.month = substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) END) AS net_gbp
  FROM sales o
  LEFT JOIN order_value v ON v.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_refunds r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)
),
with_prev AS (
  SELECT month, net_gbp, LAG(net_gbp) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_gbp FROM monthly
)
SELECT month, net_gbp AS net_revenue_gbp, 100.0 * (net_gbp - prev_gbp) / prev_gbp AS change_pct
FROM with_prev
WHERE month BETWEEN '2026-01' AND '2026-06'
ORDER BY month

cases.notes: [hard] LAG over every month (including December 2025), filtered afterwards. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: filters to January–June before LAG, so January has no previous month (0.833); change as a ratio of the new month instead of the previous one (0); gross revenue in mixed currencies (no refunds, no conversion) (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Kwame (CRM): "I want the customers who'd bought from us at least twice, then had a refund, and never bought again after that first refund."

A customer qualifies when (a) they have at least two sales, (b) at least one refund was made on one of their sales, and (c) none of their sales was placed after the moment (refunded_at) of their first such refund. Return one row per customer with three columns: customer_id, full_name, and the date of their first refund as text 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
per_customer AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_sales, MAX(ordered_at) AS last_sale
  FROM sales WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id
),
first_refund AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id, MIN(r.refunded_at) AS first_refund_at
  FROM refunds r JOIN sales o ON o.order_id = r.order_id
  WHERE o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, date(f.first_refund_at) AS first_refund_on
FROM per_customer p
JOIN first_refund f ON f.customer_id = p.customer_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
WHERE p.n_sales >= 2 AND p.last_sale <= f.first_refund_at

cases.notes: [hard] Per-customer aggregates of sales and of refunds (by refund time), compared. Planted: loyal customers whose last purchase is refunded, customers with refunds followed by more purchases, refunds on deleted duplicate orders. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: compares with the LAST refund instead of the first (0.742); counts cancelled and mistaken orders as purchases (0.763); only checks that the refunded order was their last order (ignores the refund date) (0.681).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Ines (buying): "Which two products are most often bought together? I'm planning a bundle."

Look at the sales placed from 1 January to 30 June 2026. A pair of different products is "bought together" in a sale when both appear on that sale (a product on two lines of the same sale still counts once). Find the pair (or pairs, if several are tied) that appear together in the most sales. Return one row per such pair with three columns: the name of the product with the lower product_id, the name of the other product, and the number of sales containing both.

expected.reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (o.customer_id IS NULL OR (c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL))
),
sale_products AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, oi.product_id
  FROM order_items oi JOIN sales o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-07-01'
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.product_id AS p1, b.product_id AS p2, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM sale_products a JOIN sale_products b ON b.order_id = a.order_id AND a.product_id < b.product_id
  GROUP BY a.product_id, b.product_id
)
SELECT x.name, y.name, p.n
FROM pairs p
JOIN products x ON x.product_id = p.p1
JOIN products y ON y.product_id = p.p2
WHERE p.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM pairs)

cases.notes: [hard] Distinct (sale, product) first, then a self-join with a.product_id < b.product_id, keeping every pair tied for the most. Planted: gas canisters often appear on two lines of one sale. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts line pairs, so a product on two lines counts twice (0); LIMIT 1 drops tied pairs (0.625); every order, including cancelled and test ones (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Siobhan (Trailhead Club): "Which members churned in Q1 2026 - their membership ended and they didn't come back within a month?"

Look at the real customers' subscriptions whose ended_on falls between 2026-01-01 and 2026-03-31 inclusive. Such an ending is NOT churn when the same customer has another subscription that started on or before (ended_on + 30 days) and that had not itself ended by the old ended_on (its ended_on is NULL or later than the old ended_on) - that covers switching plans, overlapping renewals and coming back within 30 days. Every other such ending is churn. Return one row per churned ending with three columns: customer_id, full_name and the ended_on date ('YYYY-MM-DD').

expected.reference:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, s.ended_on
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE c.is_test = 0 AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND s.ended_on >= '2026-01-01' AND s.ended_on <= '2026-03-31'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions t
    WHERE t.customer_id = s.customer_id
      AND t.subscription_id <> s.subscription_id
      AND t.started_on <= date(s.ended_on, '+30 days')
      AND (t.ended_on IS NULL OR t.ended_on > s.ended_on)
  )

cases.notes: [hard] Correlated NOT EXISTS with an inclusive +30-day window and an overlap condition. Planted: a return after exactly 30 days (not churn), after 31 days (churn), and a new plan that started before the old one ended (not churn). Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: only a new subscription starting after the end counts as coming back (misses early switches) (0.383); a 30-day window that excludes the 30th day (0.729); every ending in Q1 counts as churn (0.292).

scorer.schema:
CREATE TABLE stores (
  store_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  city       TEXT,            -- NULL for the website
  currency   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'GBP' or 'EUR' (the Dublin shop sells in euros)
  opened_on  TEXT NOT NULL    -- 'YYYY-MM-DD'
);
CREATE TABLE staff (
  staff_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  store_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stores(store_id),  -- the shop the person belongs to
  full_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  role       TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'manager', 'sales' or 'stock'
  manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES staff(staff_id),  -- NULL for managers
  started_on TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  left_on    TEXT             -- NULL while still employed
);
CREATE TABLE customers (
  customer_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  full_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
  email        TEXT NOT NULL,
  country      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'GB' or 'IE'
  signed_up_at TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  is_test      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- 1 = internal test account
  deleted_at   TEXT             -- set when the account was deleted (soft delete)
);
CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sku            TEXT NOT NULL,
  name           TEXT NOT NULL,
  category       TEXT NOT NULL,
  list_price_gbp REAL NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER REFERENCES customers(customer_id),  -- NULL for guest checkouts on the website
  store_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stores(store_id),
  staff_id    INTEGER REFERENCES staff(staff_id),  -- who served the sale in a shop; NULL for the website
  ordered_at  TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  status      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'completed', 'cancelled' or 'pending'
  currency    TEXT NOT NULL,   -- currency of every amount on this order and its refunds
  deleted_at  TEXT             -- set when the order was entered by mistake (soft delete)
);
CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
  quantity      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price    REAL NOT NULL,   -- in the order's currency
  line_discount REAL,            -- money off the whole line, in the order's currency; NULL = no discount
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, line_no)
);
CREATE TABLE refunds (
  refund_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
  refunded_at TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UK local time
  amount      REAL NOT NULL,   -- in the order's currency
  reason      TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE subscriptions (   -- Trailhead Club membership
  subscription_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
  plan            TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'monthly' or 'annual'
  price_gbp       REAL NOT NULL,   -- price per billing period (per month, or per year)
  started_on      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM-DD', first day of cover
  ended_on        TEXT             -- 'YYYY-MM-DD', first day WITHOUT cover; NULL = still running
);
CREATE TABLE fx_rates (
  month        TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'YYYY-MM'
  currency     TEXT NOT NULL,   -- only 'EUR' (there are no GBP rows)
  gbp_per_unit REAL NOT NULL,   -- pounds per euro for that calendar month
  PRIMARY KEY (month, currency)
);
